root_causes: Attempted Pick action when the robot was not yet within the effective interaction range of the credit card, indicating insufficient precondition checking for grasp distance.

Navigation and manipulation were not tightly coupled, leading to a Pick being issued immediately after a navigation command without confirming that the pose relative to the object was adequate for grasping.
improvement_suggestions: Add or tighten precondition checks before Pick actions to verify that the agent is within a valid distance and orientation relative to the target object, using up-to-date pose information.
Introduce a short local repositioning/align step near the object (e.g., fine navigation or approach behavior) before issuing Pick, instead of directly picking after a coarse Navigate.
Use feedback from failed Pick attempts to trigger immediate local replanning around the object (e.g., adjust position and retry) rather than just re-issuing high-level navigation.
Refine the navigation-to-object policy so that the final waypoint places the gripper within an empirically validated grasp zone around small objects like credit cards.
overall_assessment: The task was ultimately completed successfully, but there was a notable failed pick due to inadequate positioning before grasping, indicating room for improvement in the coordination between navigation and manipulation near the target object.
task_instruction: Take the credit card from the hallway to the bedroom and put it on the bedside table.
